root_cause.text: The fec_decode_bufs() function assumed that the parity bytes needed for each RS codeword are always contained within a single parity block, but due to alignment between the parity data offset and the parity block size, the parity bytes can span across two blocks, leading to an out-of-bounds read when the code reads beyond the end of the first block.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "fec_decode_bufs() assumes that the parity bytes of the first RS codeword it decodes are never split across parity blocks." It then provides an example where with block_size=4096, roots=17, nbufs=1, on the 16th call the alignment is 4080 bytes into the first block, only 16 bytes remain but 17 parity bytes are needed, causing an out-of-bounds read. The patch refactors the parity reading logic to copy 'roots' bytes, reading another parity block when the current block is exhausted, as shown in the diff where new code handles parity_pos and to_copy to cross block boundaries.

vuln_statements.content: par = fec_read_parity(v, rsb, block_offset, &offset, par_buf_offset, &buf, bio->bi_ioprio);

candidates.rationale: This call obtains a pointer to a parity block and sets offset. It assumes that all needed parity bytes for the upcoming RS codewords are contained within the returned block, but due to alignment, they may span multiple blocks.

This loop condition determines the number of bytes to copy from the parity block. It does not verify that offset + j stays within the block, so if the parity data crosses a boundary, it reads beyond the block's end.
This is the direct out-of-bounds read. When offset + j exceeds v->fec->io_size, it reads memory beyond the allocated block, causing the vulnerability.

After processing each RS block, offset is advanced. If the initial offset was near the end of the block, this can push offset beyond the block size. The subsequent check for split parity bytes (line 141) may not adequately prevent the next read from going out of bounds.

It does not handle the case where the very first set of parity bytes (processed immediately after the initial fec_read_parity) already spans across a boundary, leaving a gap in protection.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the fix for the OOB read when parity bytes span two blocks. In fec_decode_bufs(), a local buffer `par_buf` is introduced, and the code copies the split parity bytes into it (line `memcpy(&par_buf[par_buf_offset], &par[offset], v->fec->roots - par_buf_offset);`). Then `fec_decode_rs8` is called using `par_buf` instead of directly from the dm-bufio block, preventing out-of-bounds access. The logic at the end of the loop (checking `if (offset < v->fec->io_size && (offset + v->fec->roots) > v->fec->io_size)`) explicitly handles the split, setting `par_buf_offset` for the next block. Additionally, `verity_fec_ctr` now always sets `f->io_size = 1 << v->data_dev_block_bits`, removing the problematic conditional that could lead to misalignment. Thus the vulnerable construct is no longer present, and the fix is fully applied.
